_: The Genesis app catalogue: one good answer per need, with a reason. Read by genesis-apps and by the assistant. kind: here = in the image already; flatpak = from Flathub, per user; toolbox = a distrobox with a toolchain, made on first use. Nothing on this list is a system change.

apps.title: Firefox
apps.why: The browser that ships; already here.

apps.title: Chromium
apps.why: For the sites that only work in Chrome; no Google account baked in. Already here.

apps.title: Brave
apps.why: Chrome's engine with ads and trackers blocked out of the box.

apps.title: LibreOffice
apps.why: Writer, Calc, Impress; opens Word and Excel files. Installed on first connection.

apps.title: ONLYOFFICE
apps.why: If you live in .docx and want it to look exactly like it does in Word.

apps.title: Obsidian
apps.why: Notes as plain Markdown files in a folder you own; the assistant can read them.

apps.title: Joplin
apps.why: Notes that sync through Nextcloud or Dropbox, open source, with a phone app.

apps.title: Okular
apps.why: PDFs, with annotation and form filling; already here.

apps.title: Calibre
apps.why: Every e-book you have, in one library, converted to whatever your reader wants.

apps.title: Thunderbird
apps.why: Mail, calendar and contacts. Installed on first connection.

apps.title: Signal
apps.why: The messenger to use when it matters who can read it.

apps.title: Telegram
apps.why: Fast, good on a desktop, and where a lot of groups already are.

apps.title: Discord
apps.why: Voice and text for communities and games.

apps.title: Slack
apps.why: For the workplace that uses it.

apps.title: Element
apps.why: Matrix: chat you can host yourself, end-to-end encrypted.

apps.title: Zoom
apps.why: For the meetings you did not choose the software for.

apps.title: VLC
apps.why: Plays anything. Installed on first connection.

apps.title: Haruna
apps.why: The video player that fits this desktop; already here.

apps.title: Elisa
apps.why: Your music folder as a library; already here.

apps.title: Spotify
apps.why: The official client.

apps.title: Jellyfin Media Player
apps.why: Your own Netflix, if you run a Jellyfin server.

apps.title: GIMP
apps.why: Photo editing and retouching. Installed on first connection.

apps.title: Krita
apps.why: Painting and drawing with a tablet. Installed on first connection.

apps.title: Inkscape
apps.why: Vector graphics: logos, icons, diagrams, anything that must scale.

apps.title: darktable
apps.why: RAW photos, developed like in a darkroom, non-destructively.

apps.title: Blender
apps.why: 3D, animation, video editing; the whole studio.

apps.title: Kdenlive
apps.why: Video editing that fits this desktop and handles real projects.

apps.title: OBS Studio
apps.why: Recording the screen and streaming.

apps.title: Audacity
apps.why: Recording and cutting audio.

apps.title: HandBrake
apps.why: Converting video to a size and format that plays everywhere.

apps.title: Kate
apps.why: The editor that ships, with LSP and a terminal; already here.

apps.title: Visual Studio Code
apps.why: The editor most people use; Microsoft's build, with its telemetry.

apps.title: VSCodium
apps.why: VS Code without the telemetry and the Microsoft branding.

apps.title: Zed
apps.why: A fast editor built for pairing, with local models.

apps.title: Node.js toolbox
apps.why: node and npm in a box of their own; your home is shared, the OS is not touched.

apps.title: Rust toolbox
apps.why: cargo, rustc and gcc in a box of their own.

apps.title: DBeaver
apps.why: One client for every database.

apps.title: Bruno
apps.why: An API client whose collections are files in git, not in somebody's cloud.

apps.title: Podman Desktop
apps.why: Containers with a window, on the podman that is already here.

apps.title: Bitwarden
apps.why: Passwords, synced, open source, with a free tier that is enough.

apps.title: KeePassXC
apps.why: Passwords in one encrypted file you keep yourself; no account anywhere.

apps.title: Nextcloud
apps.why: Sync your files with your own server.

apps.title: LocalSend
apps.why: AirDrop between anything on the same network, no account.

apps.title: Warp
apps.why: Send a file to anyone with a code, over the internet, encrypted.

apps.title: qBittorrent
apps.why: Torrents without ads.

apps.title: Remmina
apps.why: Remote desktops: RDP, VNC, SSH in one place.

apps.title: Flatseal
apps.why: See and change what each Flatpak app is allowed to touch.

apps.title: Steam
apps.why: Most Windows games run through Proton; check protondb.com for yours.

apps.title: Heroic
apps.why: Epic, GOG and Amazon games, one launcher.

apps.title: Bottles
apps.why: Windows programs that are not games, each in its own bottle.
